extraction.name: Microsoft COCO: Common Objects in Context
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for detecting and segmenting objects found in everyday life in their natural environments. Contains 91 common object categories with 2.5 million labeled instances in 328,000 images. Objects are labeled using per-instance segmentations to aid in precise object localization. The dataset emphasizes non-iconic images containing objects in their natural context with rich contextual relationships.
extraction.creator: Tsung-Yi Lin, Michael Maire, Serge Belongie, Lubomir Bourdev, Ross Girshick, James Hays, Pietro Perona, Deva Ramanan, C. Lawrence Zitnick, Piotr Dollár
extraction.publisher: Microsoft Research / Cornell NYC Tech / Facebook AI Research / Toyota Technological Institute at Chicago / Brown University / California Institute of Technology / University of California at Irvine
extraction.citeAs: T. Lin, M. Maire, S. Belongie, J. Hays, P. Perona, D. Ramanan, P. Dollár, and C. L. Zitnick, 'Microsoft COCO: Common objects in context,' in ECCV, 2014.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were collected from Flickr by searching for pairs of object categories (e.g., 'dog + car') and scene/object category pairs to obtain non-iconic images with rich contextual relationships. At most 5 photos taken by a single photographer within a short time window were downloaded. In rare cases where enough images could not be found, single category searches were used with explicit filtering to remove iconic images. An Amazon Mechanical Turk filtering task was used to remove invalid or iconic images from candidate sets.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: 11 categories were omitted from the 2014 release: hat, shoe, eyeglasses (too many instances), mirror, window, door, street sign (ambiguous and difficult to label), plate, desk (due to confusion with bowl and dining table, respectively), and blender, hair brush (too few instances).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images collected from Flickr using pairwise object category queries and scene/object category pairs. The dataset contains 328,000 images depicting complex everyday scenes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: First half released in 2014, second half released in 2015.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Near-duplicate images were explicitly removed (detected with Douze et al. 2009 method) and images were grouped by photographer and date taken to minimize near-duplicates across splits. Images containing more than 10-15 instances of a category had remaining instances marked as 'crowds' using a single segment.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Candidate images were filtered to remove iconic and invalid images via an AMT filtering task. Near-duplicate images were removed. Images were split into training, validation, and test sets (approximately 1/2 train, 1/4 val, 1/4 test for the 2014 release). The 2014 release was limited to 80 of the 91 categories. Object categories were selected through a hierarchical voting process by co-authors, starting from 272 candidate categories down to 91 final categories.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-stage annotation pipeline was used via Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT): (1) Category Labeling - workers used a hierarchical approach grouping 91 categories into 11 super-categories, dragging icons onto object instances; 8 workers labeled each image (20k worker hours total). (2) Instance Spotting - workers placed crosses on all instances of each identified category, with up to 10 instances per category per image; 8 workers per image (10k worker hours total). (3) Instance Segmentation - workers segmented each object instance using a modified OpenSurfaces interface; workers required to pass a training task per category before annotating; segmentations verified by 3-5 additional workers, with those not receiving at least 4/5 favorable votes discarded (over 22 worker hours per 1,000 segmentations). Five written caption descriptions were also added to each image.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT); modified OpenSurfaces project interface for instance segmentation
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Worker quality on category labeling was analyzed by comparing to seven expert workers (co-authors). The union of 8 AMT workers achieved greater recall than any individual expert. Worker recall saturates at around 9-10 AMT workers. A leave-one-out evaluation procedure was used to assess individual worker precision and recall. Workers below a precision threshold were rejected. For segmentation, workers consistently producing poor segmentations had all their work discarded. Approximately 1 in 3 workers passed the segmentation training stage.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 8 workers for category labeling and instance spotting; 1 worker per instance segmentation with 3-5 workers for verification; 5 caption descriptions per image
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset was released in two halves: the first half in 2014 (82,783 training, 40,504 validation, 40,775 testing images) and the second half in 2015 (cumulative total of 165,482 train, 81,208 val, 81,434 test images). MS COCO will evolve and grow over time; up-to-date information is available at http://mscoco.org/. Funding provided by Microsoft.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of people in everyday scenes, including approximately 270k segmented person instances in the 2014 train+val data.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to advance the state-of-the-art in object recognition and scene understanding by providing richly annotated images of common objects in natural contexts. It enables the development of more robust object detection and segmentation algorithms that generalize better to real-world scenarios.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses only on 'thing' categories and not 'stuff' categories (sky, street, grass), which may limit contextual information. The selection of 91 categories was based on votes by co-authors and frequency of occurrence, which may introduce selection bias. Images were primarily sourced from Flickr, which may reflect the demographics and interests of Flickr users.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset only includes 'thing' categories and not 'stuff' categories. The 2014 release is limited to 80 of the 91 categories (11 categories omitted due to too many instances, ambiguity, difficulty of labeling, or too few instances). For images with more than 10-15 instances of a category, remaining instances are marked as 'crowds' and ignored during evaluation. Object-part categories (face, hands, wheels) are not included. The dataset does not include fine-grained categories.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing for object detection and instance segmentation algorithms. The dataset is designed for: detecting non-iconic views of objects, contextual reasoning between objects, and precise 2D localization of objects. Baseline performance analysis provided using Deformable Parts Model for bounding box and segmentation detection.
